answer: A staking-backed reputation vault makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it lied or double-spent. New identities start with a low trust limit, so an attacker cannot simply invent a fable of many trustworthy traders; each ivory-tower persona still needs its own stake, time, and successful history. Creating thousands of Sybils therefore costs thousands of deposits, while honest agents keep one stake and build reputation cheaply.
